findings.title: Wazuh VPN proxy socket boot race is not fixed: systemd still deletes the socket jobs on boot (listeners dead 45 min after the Oct 11 reboot)
findings.note: Post-run 2026-10-11: boot race fixed in main (PR #55) - wg ordering removed + FreeBind=yes on both proxy sockets; freebind capability proven live on this systemd (bound an unassigned address); listeners up 10.99.0.1:15140/15141; next reboot is the final proof. | verify 2026-10-12: `config/systemd/falcon-wazuh-{agent,enroll}-proxy.socket:12` `FreeBind=yes`, wg ordering removed (`3b0b976`); live units match, active, listeners 10.99.0.1:15140/15141
findings.detail: At the 2026-10-11T02:27:44Z boot systemd logged 'sockets.target: Found ordering cycle on falcon-wazuh-enroll-proxy.socket/start ... dependency on wg-quick@wg0.service/start ... Job falcon-wazuh-enroll-proxy.socket/start deleted to break ordering cycle' (same for -agent-). Both listeners were absent until 03:13:02Z, when a verification session ran systemctl enable/start by hand (sudo journal). The socket start history shows the same pattern at the 2026-10-01 01:47Z boot (job deleted; listener up 03:21:32Z) and on 2026-09-30. The 2026-09-30 fix (WantedBy=multi-user.target) does not break the cycle because the socket keeps its implicit Before=sockets.target (DefaultDependencies) plus After=wg-quick@wg0.service, and wg-quick@wg0 is ordered After=basic.target (which pulls sockets.target); systemd still resolves the cycle by deleting the socket start job. The remote Wazuh agent was disconnected 02:44-03:15Z as a direct consequence. The new alert rule falcon-wazuh-proxy-listeners (PR #53, live) now detects the condition in ~10 min, but the boot path remains broken and docs/runbooks/VPN.md:193 still says 'fixed 2026-09-30'. Fix: remove the cycle at the unit level (e.g. DefaultDependencies=no + explicit Before=multi-user.target, or start the proxies after wg0 via a dependent unit), add the socket state to the read-only boot check, correct the runbook.

findings.title: Ingest contract relies on a shared secret header, not request signing or idempotency keys
findings.note: verify 2026-10-12: Ingest is still shared-secret HTTP basic auth (`config/vector/aggregator.yaml:25-28`, `config/vector/edge.yaml:245-248`); no HMAC/nonce/idempotency key anywhere (`git log f5cb7c9..HEAD -- config/vector/` empty). Duplicates measured, not prevented.
findings.detail: The edge->aggregator ingest path (POST http://vector-aggregator:6000/) is authenticated only by HTTP basic auth with a shared secret (falcon-vector-edge/${VECTOR_INGEST_PW}); there is no per-request signature, timestamp/nonce or idempotency key, so a party holding the secret can inject or replay telemetry and retries create duplicates. Duplicates are measured (falcon_pipeline_duplicate_ratio, live 0.0000 over a 2000-event sample) but not prevented. Unchanged between 08e20d1 and f5cb7c9. Fix: add an HMAC (or mTLS) request signature with a timestamp/nonce and an idempotency key mapped to a deterministic document _id, keeping basic auth as a second factor.

findings.title: Pipeline counters rule fires on benign edge_ingest HTTP method rejections and the lazily-registered Vector counters vanish, producing a counter reset inside the firing window
findings.note: Post-run 2026-10-11: edge_ingest HTTP method rejections excluded from the data-loss error sum and exported separately (falcon_pipeline_edge_ingest_errors_total; PR #55). | verify 2026-10-12: `export_monitor_metrics.sh:85-90` excludes `edge_ingest` errors from the loss sum, exported separately `:534-536`; live `falcon_pipeline_edge_ingest_errors_total 0`, `falcon_pipeline_all_errors_total 0`; no firing since 2026-10-11T04:21Z
findings.detail: The rule falcon-pipeline-discarded-events (bootstrap/90-alerting.sh:246-248) sums increases of falcon_pipeline_all_discarded_events_total and falcon_pipeline_all_errors_total. On 2026-10-11 it fired 04:10:25Z -> RESOLVED 04:21:25Z because falcon_pipeline_all_errors_total went 0 -> 2 (04:05Z) -> 4 (04:06-04:12Z) -> 0 (from 04:13Z); the discarded counter stayed 0 (no loss). The trigger was source-level HTTP method rejections on the ingest listener ('ERROR source{component_id=edge_ingest component_type=http_server} ... Rejection([MethodNotAllowed, MethodNotAllowed])' at 04:03:42-04:04:54Z). The underlying Vector series are lazily registered and disappear when idle: the raw 127.0.0.1:9598 exposition now has no vector_component_errors_total or vector_component_discarded_events_total series, so the exporter (export_monitor_metrics.sh:84-85,505-509) writes 0 and Prometheus records a reset (resets(...[1h]) = 1); increase(...[15m]) was still 2.03 at 04:20Z with the counter at 0, sustaining the firing ~8 minutes past the errors. Fix: exclude source-level HTTP rejections from the loss signal (or add a separate rejection counter), and document the reset behavior; consider a stable gauge for last-window loss.

Fix: add a runtime bound (RuntimeMaxSec or a watchdog) and a stuck-run alert, and consider a textfile-based check of critical unit states.

findings.title: Data-LV warning/reclaim thresholds remain GiB constants that sit above OpenSearch's default watermarks on a 224 GiB volume

findings.detail: falcon-data-lv-low fires below 15 GiB free (bootstrap/90-alerting.sh:538-540) = 93.3% used on the 224 GiB data LV, and the disk guard reclaims only below 10 GiB (automation/validation/disk_guard.sh:22) = 95.5% used, while OpenSearch's watermarks are back to defaults (live _cluster/settings: persistent contains only ISM metadata, transient {}; defaults low 85% / high 90% / flood 95% with the single-node enable retained - DR-P2-001 verified-fixed). On a 224 GiB LV the engine's first write refusal (flood 95% = 11.2 GiB free) precedes the guard's reclaim (10 GiB free), and the warning (15 GiB = 93.3%) sits after the high watermark (90% = 22.4 GiB free). Data LV is currently 55% used / 96 GiB free, so the mismatch is latent; the constants are still volume-independent literals with no CI check tying guard/alert thresholds to the engine watermarks.
